=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1505-1507 (guard_deletion_pattern) and 1531-1562 (cross-file scan plus `if cross_file_guard_deleted: return True`) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The cross-file tripwire treats unrelated deleted control-flow lines or common tokens such as `allow`, `deny`, `policy`, `role`, `admin`, and `auth*` anywhere in the project diff as proof that every finding is project-owned.
  WHY: This reclassifies provably base-owned findings as blocking and defeats `SECURITY_PASS_LINE_OWNERSHIP=project-lines`; the reviewers agree on the false-positive behavior, while moonshotai_kimi-k3 recommends limiting the cross-file scan to guard-shaped deletions.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1614-1621 (per-file causal loop with `has_context_name`, `has_control_change`, `has_guard_deletion`) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The per-file ownership rule marks every finding in a cited file as project-owned when any unrelated hunk in that file contains a deletion plus a control-flow or guard-token deletion.
  WHY: The cited line's relationship to the deletion is never checked, so unrelated changes cause base-owned findings to become blocking and consume security-pass fix cycles.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1505-1507 (guard_deletion_pattern), 1544-1562 (cross-file scan and `if cross_file_guard_deleted: return True`), 1614-1621 (per-file hunk rule) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: Custom authorization guards such as `check_entitlement(user)`, `verify_tenant()`, or deleted decorators outside the fixed keyword vocabulary can escape both ownership rules and route a project-introduced bypass to a non-blocking advisory.
  WHY: The detector recognizes only a fixed set of guard names; the new regression test covers `@login_required` but not unknown-named guards.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1388-1389 (`fail(f"{finding_id}: tracked file path cannot be encoded safely ...")`) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A single valid tracked filename containing glob or special characters causes `fail()` to terminate the entire audit process.
  WHY: The output file is left unwritten and all other findings in the batch are lost instead of only suppressing the unrepresentable finding.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1402-1428 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `git blame` fails and `audit_scope_head_sha` is empty or invalid, findings are classified as invalid and can be discarded without failing the security pass.
  WHY: A non-git or git-broken checkout can produce an empty findings payload that the poller accepts as clean even though no review was completed.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1531-1542 (`git diff … {audit_scope_base_sha}..{audit_scope_head_sha}` for cross-file causal scan) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The cross-file scan always evaluates the full `base..head` range instead of honoring narrowed delta-audit scope.
  WHY: Deleted guards outside the current re-audit range continue to affect current findings, and the cross-file cache cannot avoid the stale full-range result.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1551 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The cross-file scan performs regex work across the remaining full diff after its boolean result is already known.
  WHY: Large diffs can impose unnecessary CPU cost; moonshotai_kimi-k3 disputes this finding, stating the predicate uses a short-circuiting generator and that the subprocess capture is the bounded cost.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:2038-2046 (followup dedup condition `waiver_match_key in existing_waiver_keys or (not waiver_match_key and finding_id in existing_finding_ids)`) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A fresh keyless finding can be suppressed solely because its model-generated display ID collides with an existing legacy issue.
  WHY: Display IDs are not authoritative, so the fallback can silently hide a distinct advisory and prevent its waiver from being created.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1595 (`has_context_name` extraction), 1614 (tuple unpacking) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `has_context_name` is extracted and stored in every hunk tuple but never consumed by the ownership decision.
  WHY: The dead field is misleading maintenance data and does not affect runtime routing.
- CI signal only — check-run `codex-agent` (run 35531058308) completed with conclusion `cancelled`; failed[0].summary and failed[0].log_tail are empty. | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: A cancelled check-run is reported without log content or a code-site mapping.
  WHY: The cancellation may be a concurrency-superseded sibling run, but the artifact does not establish that.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:1348-1349 (`finding_id = "finding-" + hashlib.sha256(...)` canonicalization) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: Model-reported finding IDs containing characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` are replaced by opaque hashes and the original readable ID is discarded.
  WHY: Operator-facing triage and `/security-pass-waive <finding_id>` surfaces can no longer correlate the hash to the model-emitted identifier.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A project can delete an authorization guard while leaving the privileged sink unchanged beyond the blame window. The resulting project-introduced bypass is classified as pre-existing and non-blocking. Include deleted diff hunks and enclosing control-flow changes in ownership analysis; keep findings blocking unless their causal code is provably base-owned." (from linked issue #4173, `line-ownership-misses-deleted-guards` row)
  expected_change_site: scripts/security_audit.sh, `finding_is_project_owned` function
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: The cross-file deleted-guard detection at lines 1505-1562 only recognizes a fixed keyword vocabulary; custom guards such as `check_entitlement(user)`, `@rate_limit`, or `verify_tenant()` are not recognized, and `test_security_audit_cross_file_deleted_guard_keeps_sink_blocking` only exercises `@login_required`.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1544-1556 (cross-file scan), 1561-1562 (guard-deleted return)
  Problem: The cross-file scan makes every project-lines ownership finding blocking when any deleted control-flow keyword or guard-like token appears anywhere in the diff.
  Why it fails at runtime: Unrelated refactors or common tokens trigger fix cycles and can terminalize the project despite base-owned defects.
  severity=high | confidence=4
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1402-1428
  Problem: Findings are dropped as invalid when Git provenance cannot be derived and the audit head SHA is unavailable.
  Why it fails at runtime: The poller can record a clean security pass with no actual review.
  severity=high | confidence=3
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1388-1389
  Problem: An unsafe-but-legally-named tracked path raises `SystemExit` and aborts the complete audit.
  Why it fails at runtime: `findings.json` is not written and all findings in the model batch are lost.
  severity=high | confidence=3
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1614-1621
  Problem: Any deletion plus control or guard deletion anywhere in the cited file marks unrelated findings as project-owned.
  Why it fails at runtime: Unrelated hunks trigger unnecessary blocking fix cycles.
  severity=low | confidence=3
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1551
  Problem: The cross-file scan performs eager per-line regex processing across the complete diff after the result is known.
  Why it fails at runtime: Large integration diffs incur unnecessary CPU cost.
  severity=low | confidence=4
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "A project can delete an authorization guard while leaving the privileged sink unchanged beyond the blame window. The resulting project-introduced bypass is classified as pre-existing and non-blocking. Include deleted diff hunks and enclosing control-flow changes in ownership analysis; keep findings blocking unless their causal code is provably base-owned." (from linked issue #4173, `line-ownership-misses-deleted-guards` row)
  Expected change site: scripts/security_audit.sh, `finding_is_project_owned` function
  Evidence of absence: The cross-file detector recognizes only a fixed vocabulary; custom authorization guards are missed, and the regression test covers only `@login_required`.
  severity=high | confidence=4

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1505-1507 (guard_deletion_pattern) and 1531-1562 (cross-file scan plus `if cross_file_guard_deleted: return True`)
  Problem: Common control-flow and authorization-like deletions anywhere in the project diff classify every finding as project-owned.
  Why it fails at runtime: `SECURITY_PASS_LINE_OWNERSHIP=project-lines` silently degrades to file-level blocking and consumes fix cycles on base-owned defects.
  severity=high | confidence=4
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1614-1621 (per-file causal loop with `has_context_name`, `has_control_change`, `has_guard_deletion`)
  Problem: Any qualifying hunk in a cited file reclassifies findings in unrelated functions.
  Why it fails at runtime: Unrelated changes trigger blocking fix cycles.
  severity=high | confidence=4
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1388-1389 (`fail(f"{finding_id}: tracked file path cannot be encoded safely ...")`)
  Problem: `fail()` aborts the complete child process for one legal filename containing special characters.
  Why it fails at runtime: The poller sees no output file and the whole audit fails closed.
  severity=high | confidence=3
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1531-1542 (`git diff … {audit_scope_base_sha}..{audit_scope_head_sha}` for cross-file causal scan)
  Problem: The cross-file scan ignores narrowed delta-audit scope and always scans the full range.
  Why it fails at runtime: Stale deleted-guard matches continue to misclassify later re-audit findings.
  severity=low | confidence=4
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1595 (`"has_context_name": bool(hunk_match.group(3).strip())` inside the per-file hunk parser)
  Problem: `has_context_name` is dead data in the hunk tuple.
  Why it fails at runtime: No direct failure, but the unused signal misleads future ownership changes.
  severity=low | confidence=4
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 1427-1428 (`return None, f"{finding_id}: unable to derive immutable Git provenance for cited line"`)
  Problem: Provenance failures are converted into suppressed invalid findings.
  Why it fails at runtime: A checkout without usable Git metadata can be reported clean with zero real findings.
  severity=high | confidence=3
- scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: 2038-2046 (followup dedup condition `waiver_match_key in existing_waiver_keys or (not waiver_match_key and finding_id in existing_finding_ids)`)
  Problem: A keyless finding can be suppressed by a colliding legacy display ID.
  Why it fails at runtime: A fresh advisory is silently omitted and repeatedly re-emitted later.
  severity=low | confidence=3
